newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industrialists paint rosy outlook for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industrialists paint rosy outlook for 1997.

text.p: The outlook for Brazil's economy in 1997 is rosy on all fronts with falling inflation, faster growth and rising industrial production, according to the private National Industry Confederation (CNI).

The CNI said annual inflation would fall further in 1997 to reach a single digit rate, while economic growth in 1997 would be higher than this year and the recovery in industrial production was consolidating in the third quarter of 1996.
The CNI also forecast an improvement in next year's public sector deficit due to an expected increase in privatization receipts.

The main economic indicators, as well as the government's efforts to reduce the cost of doing business in Brazil and to speed up the privatization process, contributed to the favorable outlook, the CNI said in a statement.
The CNI said the greatest risks for the Brazilian economy lay beyond its borders, including any substantial changes in the Argentine economy or international interest rates.
The CNI also sees dangers in the Brazilian political arena.

"There are also risks in the political scenario, mainly with regard to the non-approval of the (constitutional) amendment on (presidential) re-election, which could introduce a degree of instability in the macroeconomic area," the CNI said.
The CNI said it was important that the positive outlook for next year would not lead the government to neglect its efforts in the fiscal domain which required serious reforms.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
